headline: Law keeps interest from federal taxes on guns, ammunition, and archery gear going to wetlands conservation programs through fiscal year 2033.
what_it_does: Federal excise taxes on certain firearms, ammunition, and archery equipment go into a wildlife fund, and that money earns interest. This law extends a rule that sends the interest to wildlife conservation and restoration programs set up under the North American Wetlands Conservation Act. The rule was set to end at the start of fiscal year 2026 and now runs through fiscal year 2033. Without the extension, the interest would have gone to states by formula for wildlife restoration, hunter education and safety, multistate conservation grants, and administrative costs.

who_it_affects.group: Groups and projects funded under the North American Wetlands Conservation Act
who_it_affects.how: They continue to receive the interest earned on the wildlife fund through fiscal year 2033.
They will not receive this interest money through the state formula for wildlife restoration, hunter education, and related uses while the extension is in place.

who_it_affects.group: People who buy firearms, ammunition, or archery equipment
who_it_affects.how: The law does not change the taxes they pay, only where the interest earned on that tax money goes.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted November 25, 2025; the extension covers fiscal years 2026 through 2033.
